criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately reflects all governance rules and authority requirements from the operative sources. Specifically, it applies the approved in-force rule from record-17.txt (requiring Finance controllers, Program Managers, and Purchase teams to approve every price-change request) and explicitly rejects the unapproved draft in record-22.txt (Purchase-only approval). It also preserves the required TRSO signoffs (ER, Quality, and Purchase) and supplier nomination signoffs (Finance, Quality, ER, and Program Managers) from the request, clearly frames the new routing and change lanes as a proposal rather than existing approved policy, states open assumptions/decisions without inventing facts, and sends no external communications.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
The registry, not recency alone, determines which record is operative.
evidence.output_quote: Price-change approval: Finance controllers, Program Managers and Purchase must all approve every price-change request; Purchase-only approval is not permitted.

evidence.source_quote: Price change request approvals: Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams. All three are required.
evidence.output_quote: Technical approval: ER, Quality and Purchase approve TRSO revisions. Nomination approval: Finance, Quality, ER and Program Managers sign the nomination package. Price-change approval: Finance controllers, Program Managers and Purchase must all approve every price-change request; Purchase-only approval is not permitted.

evidence.source_quote: If sources disagree, apply the operative approval status. Produce the requested professional deliverables, state unresolved assumptions, and do not invent missing facts.
evidence.output_quote: CPO/process owners must confirm change-classification policy, delegation, escalation timing and retention; TechSol must confirm signature controls, security, migration and integration scope. These implementation choices do not suspend existing approval requirements.

criteria.consequence: None; operative approval authorities and source boundaries are properly maintained.
criteria.counterevidence: None found. The unapproved draft in record-22.txt was inspected and properly excluded in favor of the approved in-force record-17.txt.

criteria.rationale: The deliverable fulfills all substantive requirements of the prompt in a well-structured Word document tailored for both the CPO and TechSol teams. It defines the end-to-end sourcing workflow and decision gates (G1 through G6), specifies the plug-and-play modular quotation structure covering features, design elements, child parts, and raw materials, establishes post-nomination flexibility lanes (Lanes A, B, and C) to handle late design changes without losing traceability, details the approval layers and functional accountabilities, and provides a clear digital platform blueprint and pilot plan for TechSol.

evidence.source_quote: Revised sourcing and nomination workflow must involve a ‘Modular quotation structure’ to develop a plug-and-play model for cost drivers based on features, design elements, child parts and raw material used. Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes.
evidence.output_quote: Define a stable base assembly plus selectable modules for features, design elements, child parts and raw materials. Illustrative lamp modules include lighting functions, optical elements, housing/appearance options, electronics and connectors.

evidence.source_quote: As a first step, the CPO has asked you to develop the first-level workflow draft for this new sourcing process — both as a strategic process recommendation and as the foundational blueprint for the digital platform the TechSol will build.
evidence.output_quote: Core records: program, part/variant, supplier, TRSO revision, evaluation, module/BOM, quotation revision, negotiation event, nomination baseline, change request, approval and commercial release. Use persistent IDs and explicit links so any price can be traced to its configuration, quote, negotiation and approvals.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable is complete and ready for executive and technical review.

task_defect.reason: The request and workspace records are clear, consistent, and unambiguous regarding operative authority and deliverable requirements.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
